newsitem.title: JAPAN: Fujitsu raises domestic PC sales target for 96/97.
newsitem.headline: Fujitsu raises domestic PC sales target for 96/97.

text.p: Fujitsu Ltd has raised its target for domestic personal computer sales in 1996/97 to 2.2 million units, up from the goal of two million it set in April, Fujitsu executive director Takeshi Maruyama said on Wednesday.
Maruyama told a news conference that Fujitsu sold 900,000 PCs in Japan in the April-September first half of the 1996/97 business year, up from 500,000 units a year ago.
In the global market, the company aims to sell three million PCs this business year, he said.
Fujitsu will aim to sell 600,000 PCs in Europe and 100,000-150,000 in the United States in 1996/97.
It began selling PCs in the U.S. market for the first time when it began selling notebook-type laptops there at the end of June this year.
Maruyama said a favourable market environment in Japan prompted Fujitsu to raise its domestic sales target.
Last business year, Fujitsu sold 1.45 million PCs in Japan.
